message.content:
**Ace in Blackjack – the “soft” card**

| What it is | How it works |
|------------|--------------|
| **Value** | An Ace can count as **11** or **1**. |
| **Primary rule** | It is first counted as 11. If that would make the hand’s total exceed 21 (a bust), the Ace automatically “drops” to 1. |
| **Why it matters** | This flexibility lets a hand stay “soft” (i.e., still able to improve without busting). For example, an Ace‑7 is a *soft 18* (11+7). If you hit and draw a 5, the Ace becomes 1, giving you 13 instead of busting. |
| **Blackjack (natural)** | An Ace plus any 10‑point card (10, J, Q, K) is a *natural Blackjack*. It usually pays 3:2 unless the dealer also has a natural, in which case it’s a push. |
| **Dealer’s rules** | The dealer must hit on a soft 17 (soft 17 = Ace + 6). Some casinos use “dealer stands on soft 17”; the rule varies by house. |
| **Splitting** | A pair of Aces can be split. Each Ace is then treated as a new starting card, and you may receive one additional card to each hand. |
| **Insurance** | If the dealer’s up‑card is an Ace, you can take insurance (a side bet that the dealer has a natural). |

**Bottom line:**  
Treat the Ace as 11 unless that would bust your hand; then treat it as 1. This dual value is what makes the Ace the most powerful card in Blackjack.
